category: Solid Mechanics features: constraints, frames and loads, springs and masses, connections, contact, bolts, fracture and result nodes
description: Boundary, domain, point and global nodes of the Solid Mechanics interface (Structural Mechanics Module and add-ons) beyond the basic set: symmetry and periodicity, accelerated/rotating frames, thin layers and spring-dampers, fasteners and attachments, contact formulations with friction, adhesion, decohesion and wear, bolt pretension, crack evaluation and stress-evaluation helpers. Type strings and parameter keys were confirmed in COMSOL 6.4 Application Library models where given.

tools.name: Symmetry Plane (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Symmetry condition for 2D axisymmetric models, where the only possible symmetry plane is normal to the Z axis. The Normal Direction Condition can be No displacement (standard symmetry), Free displacement (plane may translate with zero net reaction), Prescribed force or Prescribed displacement, which is useful for generalized plane-strain-like cuts. With circumferential displacement included, choose Symmetry or Antisymmetry for the twist component.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics (2D axisymmetric) > Boundaries > Symmetry Plane. Java: physics("solid").create("symp1", "SymmetryPlane", 1); feature("symp1").set("NormalDirectionTranslation", "NoDisplacement").

parameters.name: NormalDirectionTranslation
parameters.description: NoDisplacement, free displacement, prescribed force (Fn) or prescribed displacement (un0).

parameters.name: circumferentialCondition
parameters.description: symmetry or antisymmetry for the circumferential displacement.

tools.notes: In 3D/2D use Symmetry (solid mechanics). Application Library: Nonlinear_Structural_Materials_Module/Viscoplasticity/lemaitre_chaboche_viscoplastic_model.

tools.name: Antisymmetry (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Antisymmetry boundary condition: displacements are fixed in the plane of the boundary and free in the normal direction, the complement of a symmetry condition. Combining symmetric and antisymmetric load cases on a half model reproduces the response to arbitrary loading on the full model, and antisymmetry picks out antisymmetric eigenmodes.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Boundaries > More Constraints > Antisymmetry (also Shell, Layered Shell, Membrane edges, Beam and Truss points).

parameters.name: Constraint Settings
parameters.description: Pointwise/weak constraints and constraint group (Advanced Physics Options).

tools.example:
Solid Mechanics > Antisymmetry 1: boundary x = 0 of a half model
Study 1: Eigenfrequency with Symmetry on x = 0 (symmetric modes)
Study 2: same model with Antisymmetry on x = 0 (antisymmetric modes)
tools.notes: Large rotations must not occur on an antisymmetry plane in geometrically nonlinear analysis. Constraint groups let you switch Symmetry/Antisymmetry per load case in one study.

tools.name: Rigid Motion Suppression (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Adds the minimum set of point constraints needed to remove rigid-body modes of a free structure, chosen so that no reaction forces arise if the applied loads are self-equilibrating (e.g. pressure vessels, thermal stress in a free part, centrifugal loads). Points are picked automatically from the selected domain or explicitly (at least three in 3D, two in 2D).
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Domains > Domain Constraints > Rigid Motion Suppression. Java: physics("solid").create("rms1", "RigidMotionSuppression", 3); set("contributingPoints", "automatic").

parameters.name: contributingPoints
parameters.description: automatic (all domain points) or from selection.

tools.notes: Use one node per disconnected object and never combine with other constraints on the same object. For unbalanced loads use Inertia Relief instead. Application Library: Composite_Materials_Module/Multiphysics/heating_circuit_layered.

tools.name: Periodic Condition (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Relates displacements on a source and destination boundary set with the same shape. Types: Continuity, Antiperiodicity and User defined (any study), Floquet periodicity with a wave vector k_F (frequency domain and linear buckling of unit cells, dispersion diagrams of phononic crystals) and Cyclic symmetry with azimuthal mode number m for sectors of rotationally periodic structures such as turbine discs and impellers.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Boundaries > Periodic Condition (right-click for Manual Destination Selection). Java: physics("solid").create("pc1", "PeriodicCondition", 2); set("PeriodicType", "Floquet"); set("kFloquet", new String[]{"kx", "ky", "0"}).

parameters.name: PeriodicType
parameters.description: Continuity, antiperiodicity, Floquet, cyclic symmetry or user defined (per component via ComponentPeriodicType).

parameters.name: kFloquet
parameters.description: Floquet wave vector for Bloch-periodic unit cells.

parameters.name: mFloquet / thetaS
parameters.description: Cyclic symmetry mode number and sector angle.

parameters.name: TransformationMethod
parameters.description: How destination coordinates map to source (automatic or coordinate system based).

tools.notes: Matching meshes on source and destination (e.g. Copy Face) improve accuracy. Floquet and cyclic symmetry need the Structural Mechanics Module or others. Application Library: Structural_Mechanics_Module/Elastic_Waves/phononic_crystal and Dynamics_and_Vibration/impeller.

tools.name: Cell Periodicity (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Domain node for homogenization of a representative volume element or unit cell. Periodic (or homogeneous) boundary conditions are applied with Free expansion, Average strain, Average stress or Mixed loading (Average deformation gradient for large strains), and the node can compute the homogenized elasticity/compliance matrix, density, thermal expansion and hygroscopic swelling coefficients, optionally writing them to a new material. Boundary Pair subnodes define matched periodic faces.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Domains > Cell Periodicity; use the Automated Model Setup buttons to create load groups/studies and a homogenized material. Java: physics("solid").create("cp1", "CellPeriodicity", 3); set("BoundaryConditions", "PeriodicConditions"); set("computeElasticityMatrixStandard", "1").

parameters.name: Formulation
parameters.description: SmallStrains or large strains.

parameters.name: BoundaryConditions / BoundaryExpansion
parameters.description: Periodic or homogeneous; free expansion, prescribed average strain, average stress or mixed.

parameters.name: computeElasticityMatrixStandard/Voigt, computeThermalExpansion, computeHygroscopicSwelling, computeDensity
parameters.description: Effective properties to evaluate.

parameters.name: Volume
parameters.description: Cell volume: automatic, from void volume fraction, or user defined.

tools.notes: Used heavily in the Composite Materials Module for micromechanics (composite_multiscale). Several Cell Periodicity nodes need disjoint selections.

tools.name: Continuity (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Pair condition that glues the two sides of Identity Pairs in an assembly (Form Assembly geometry), allowing non-conforming meshes between parts. Constraint method: Pointwise (default), Nitsche (weak equations, often more accurate for mismatched meshes, symmetric, skew-symmetric or incomplete formulation) or Weak constraints; an option corrects for small gaps or overlaps between the boundaries.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Pairs > Continuity (a default Continuity node is created when identity pairs exist). Java: physics("solid").create("cont1", "Continuity", 2); set("constraintOptions", "pointwiseConstraints"); Nitsche keys: formulation (skew), stabilizationControl.

parameters.name: Pair selection
parameters.description: Identity pairs whose sides both belong to the interface.

parameters.name: Constraint method
parameters.description: Pointwise constraints, Nitsche constraints or Weak constraints.

parameters.name: Correct for mismatching boundaries
parameters.description: Compensates for gaps/overlaps between the paired faces.

parameters.name: formulation, stabilizationControl, fgamma
parameters.description: Nitsche formulation (skew/symmetric/incomplete) and stabilization factor.

tools.example:
model.component("comp1").physics("solid").create("cont1", "Continuity", 2);
// GUI: Pair Selection = Identity Pair 1 (ap1), Constraint method = Nitsche constraints
tools.notes: For connections between different interfaces (solid-shell, solid-beam) use the multiphysics couplings instead. Identity pairs are created by Form Assembly.

tools.name: Ring Load and Point Load on Axis (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Point loads in 2D axisymmetric models: a load on a point at R > 0 represents a ring load distributed around the circumference (Force per reference length, per deformed length or Total force = per-length value times 2*pi*r), whereas Point Load (on Axis) is the only true concentrated force and acts axially at R = 0. Both support Phase, Harmonic Perturbation, load groups and dead-load treatment in linear buckling.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics (2D axisymmetric) > Points > Ring Load | Point Load (on Axis). Java (on axis): physics("solid").create("pla1", "PointLoadOnAxis", 0); set("Fz", "-1[kN]").

parameters.name: Load type (Ring Load)
parameters.description: Force per reference length f_L, per deformed length f_l, or Total force F_tot.

parameters.name: Fz (Point Load on Axis)
parameters.description: Axial force.

parameters.name: treatasdeadload
parameters.description: Treat as dead load in linear buckling with live and dead loads.

tools.notes: Ring loads are also available in Shell, Membrane (edges in 2D axisymmetry). A point load at R > 0 in axisymmetry is always a ring load.

tools.name: Base Excitation (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Global node that applies a base acceleration to all constraints, mainly for mode-superposition, random vibration and response-spectrum analyses in which nonzero prescribed displacements cannot be used. Results are relative to the base; the absolute velocity and displacement solid.v_abs and solid.u_abs can be computed by integrating the base acceleration. It can be flagged as a harmonic perturbation.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Global > Base Excitation (also Pipe Mechanics, Beam, Shell, Plate). Java: physics("solid").create("bex1", "BaseExcitation", -1); set("ab", new String[]{"1[g_const]", "0", "0"}).

parameters.name: ab
parameters.description: Base acceleration vector in the selected (spatial, space-independent) coordinate system.

parameters.name: ComputeAbsoluteVelocity / ComputeAbsoluteDisplacement
parameters.description: Create absolute-motion variables.

parameters.name: harmonicPerturbation
parameters.description: Treat as a harmonic perturbation load in perturbation studies.

tools.notes: Add one Base Excitation per structural interface; it does not act on non-structural coupled physics. Constraints must be aligned with or orthogonal to the excitation direction.

tools.name: Rotating Frame (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Adds the fictitious forces of a rotating reference frame (centrifugal, Coriolis, Euler) and optional spin softening to all selected mass-carrying features, so that results are observed in the co-rotating frame. The rotation can be given as angular velocity, revolutions per time, a user-defined rotation angle alpha(t), or Rigid body with an applied moment and initial angular velocity. Used for turbine blades, flywheels, centrifuges and gyroscopes.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Domains > Rotating Frame (also Shell, Layered Shell, Multibody Dynamics). Java: physics("solid").create("rotf1", "RotatingFrame", 3); set("RotationalFrequency", "RevolutionsPerTime"); set("rpt", "3000[rpm]"); set("CoriolisForce", "1").

parameters.name: AxisOfRotation, rotaxbp, rotaxdir
parameters.description: x/y/z axis, out-of-plane axis or user-defined base point and direction.

parameters.name: RotationalFrequency
parameters.description: Angular velocity (Ovm), RevolutionsPerTime (rpt), Rigid body (M, Omega0) or user defined angle (alpha).

parameters.name: CentrifugalForce, CoriolisForce, EulerForce, SpinSoftening
parameters.description: Force contributions to include.

parameters.name: DefineSpatialFrameRotation
parameters.description: Rotate the spatial frame for visualization in the fixed frame.

tools.notes: For rotordynamics with whirl and bearings prefer the Solid Rotor interfaces. Prestressed eigenfrequency with spin softening gives speed-dependent frequencies. Application Library: Structural_Mechanics_Module/Dynamics_and_Vibration/rotating_blade.

tools.name: Linearly Accelerated Frame (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Applies inertial body forces f = -rho*a_f for a reference frame accelerating in a fixed spatial direction (vehicle acceleration, launch loads, drop tests viewed from the package). In time-dependent studies the absolute acceleration, velocity and displacement variables <phys>.<lafm>.a_abs, v_abs and u_abs can be computed.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Domains > Linearly Accelerated Frame. Java type string LinearlyAcceleratedFrame (seen with tag lafm in the Beam interface): physics("solid").create("lafm1", "LinearlyAcceleratedFrame", 3).

parameters.name: Frame acceleration a_f
parameters.description: Acceleration vector in the selected spatial coordinate system.

parameters.name: Compute absolute velocity/displacement
parameters.description: Checkboxes for postprocessing variables in time-dependent studies.

tools.notes: Only features with geometric selections contribute; global Mass and Moment of Inertia nodes do not. Response spectrum studies generate such nodes automatically (Structural_Mechanics_Module/Dynamics_and_Vibration/building_response_spectrum).

tools.name: Inertia Relief (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Enables stationary analysis of an unconstrained structure (aircraft in flight, satellites, vehicles) by assuming the external loads are balanced by rigid-body inertia. Control points are constrained so that no reaction forces occur, and up to seven extra linear load cases are solved to find the acceleration field. The Automated Model Setup creates the load groups and the dedicated study.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Domains > Inertia Relief, then Inertia Relief section toolbar > Create Load Groups and Study. Java: physics("solid").create("ire1", "InertiaRelief", 3); set("contributingPoints", "automatic").

parameters.name: contributingPoints
parameters.description: Control points: automatic or from selection (three non-collinear points in 3D, two in 2D, one off-axis in 2D axisymmetry).

tools.notes: No other boundary conditions that suppress rigid-body motion (including spring foundations) may be present. With several structural interfaces add a node to each but create the study only once.

tools.name: Hygroscopic Swelling (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Material subnode for strain caused by moisture uptake, eps_hs = beta_h*M_m*(c_mo - c_mo,ref), with isotropic or anisotropic coefficient of hygroscopic swelling. The concentration comes from a moisture or species transport interface (molar or mass concentration). Typical for paper, wood, polymers and electronic packaging exposed to humidity.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Linear Elastic Material (or other) > Hygroscopic Swelling; or Multiphysics > Hygroscopic Swelling coupling with a transport interface.

parameters.name: Concentration type
parameters.description: Molar concentration or mass concentration.

parameters.name: c_ref
parameters.description: Strain reference concentration.

parameters.name: beta_h, M_m
parameters.description: Coefficient of hygroscopic swelling (isotropic, diagonal or symmetric) and molar mass.

tools.notes: Match the discretization order of the concentration to one order below the displacement in shells. Also available in Beam, Truss and Wire. The Shrinkage and Swelling coupling handles two-way species-stress coupling.

tools.name: External Stress (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Material subnode that adds a stress contribution not given by the constitutive law, either to the total stress tensor, as a load contribution only, or as a residual stress. Stress input can be a second Piola-Kirchhoff tensor (Material), Cauchy tensor (Spatial), Nominal tensor, a Pore pressure with Biot coefficient (effective-stress soil mechanics), or an In situ stress state.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > <material> > External Stress. Java: feature("lemm1").create("exs1", "ExternalStress", 3); set("StressInputType", "PorePressure"); set("pA", "dl.p"); set("alphaB", "1").

parameters.name: StressInputType
parameters.description: StressTensorMaterial, StressTensorSpatial, StressTensorNominal, PorePressure or InSituStress.

parameters.name: ContributionType
parameters.description: Stress (add to stress tensor), load contribution only, or residual stress.

parameters.name: Sext / pA, alphaB, pref
parameters.description: External stress tensor or pore pressure, Biot-Willis coefficient and reference pressure.

tools.notes: Initial Stress and Strain always adds to the stress tensor; External Stress offers more control. Heart-muscle active stress is modelled this way in biventricular_cardiac_model.

tools.name: Enclosed Cavity (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Marks boundaries that enclose a volume and defines variables for its undeformed and deformed volume; a Fluid subnode fills it with an incompressible, compressible (isothermal/adiabatic gas or liquid with compressibility) fluid whose pressure follows an equation of state, and Prescribed Pressure applies a constant or initial overpressure. Used for seals, accumulators, tires, airbags, balloons and cardiac chambers without meshing the fluid.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Boundaries > Enclosed Cavity > Fluid / Prescribed Pressure (also Membrane). Java: physics("solid").create("enc1", "EnclosedCavity", 2); feature("enc1").create("fl1", "Fluid", 2); feature("enc1").feature("fl1").set("compressibility", "compressibleGasAdiabatic").

parameters.name: volumeType, referencePointType, X_ref
parameters.description: Closed or open surface; reference point for open surfaces (symmetry cuts).

parameters.name: fV
parameters.description: Volume factor to account for symmetry (e.g. 4 for a quarter model).

parameters.name: Fluid: compressibility, p_ref, gamma, chi_f
parameters.description: Fluid model, reference pressure, ratio of specific heats, compressibility.

parameters.name: Prescribed Pressure: p
parameters.description: Pressure inside the cavity.

tools.notes: Requires the Structural Mechanics Module. Enclosed Fluids theory covers symmetry planes and the fluid load.

tools.name: Harmonic Perturbation and Phase (Solid Mechanics Loads)
tools.description: In Frequency Domain, Prestressed (perturbation) studies only loads marked as Harmonic Perturbation act as the small harmonic excitation, while other loads define the stationary prestress. Loads get the flag through the context menu (parameter harmonicPerturbation); prescribed displacements, velocities, accelerations and rigid connectors get a Harmonic Perturbation subnode. The Phase subnode sets a load phase angle phi (radians, or [deg]) added to any complex amplitude.
tools.usage: Right-click a load (Boundary Load, Body Load, Point Load, Base Excitation...) > Harmonic Perturbation; right-click Prescribed Displacement > Harmonic Perturbation; right-click a load > Phase. Java: feature("bndl1").set("harmonicPerturbation", "1"); feature("bndl1").create("ph1", "Phase", 2).

parameters.name: harmonicPerturbation
parameters.description: Flag on load features; the load then only contributes to the perturbation step.

parameters.name: Phase phi
parameters.description: Load phase in radians per component (Phase subnode).

tools.notes: In a plain Frequency Domain study all loads are harmonic and the flag is not needed. See Small-Signal Analysis, Frequency Domain for the study.

tools.name: Thin Layer (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Models a thin elastic, damped or layered film on interior boundaries, between pair boundaries or as a cladding on exterior boundaries, without meshing its thickness. The Approximation can be Solid (full 3D stress state in the layer), Membrane (in-plane stiffness only) or Spring (Spring Material subnode). Layered thin layers take their stack from Layered Material nodes; typical uses are gaskets, adhesive bonds, coatings and electrode films.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Boundaries > Thin Layer (or Pairs > Thin Layer), with Linear Elastic/Hyperelastic/Spring Material subnodes. Java: physics("solid").create("tl1", "ThinLayer", 2); set("thicknessApproximation", "spring"); set("lth", "0.1[mm]").

parameters.name: Thin layer type
parameters.description: Nonlayered (thickness L_th) or Layered (Single Layer Material, Layered Material Link or Stack).

parameters.name: thicknessApproximation
parameters.description: Solid, membrane or spring.

parameters.name: Thickness definition (pairs)
parameters.description: User defined or From geometry (gap distance).

parameters.name: Subnodes
parameters.description: Linear Elastic, Hyperelastic, Spring Material, Fiber (Thin Layer), Fixed Constraint/Roller/Prescribed Displacement (Thin Layer).

tools.notes: Replaces the older Thin Elastic Layer for many uses; the Thermal Expansion, Thin Layer coupling provides thermal strain in layers. Only Solid approximation is available for layered thin layers.

tools.name: Spring Material (Thin Layer)
tools.description: Subnode of Thin Layer (Spring approximation) that represents the layer as distributed springs: spring constant per reference area/length, total spring constant, or force as a function of the layer extension variables <tl>.uelt1, uelt2, ueln (nonlinear springs, gap elements). Mass can be given per volume, area, length or total, and a Damping subnode adds loss.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Thin Layer (Approximation = Spring) > Spring Material. Java: feature("tl1").create("spm1", "SpringMaterial", 2); set("SpringType", "FDefTot"); set("FDefTot", new String[]{"kt*solid.tl1.uelt1", "kt*solid.tl1.uelt2", "kn*solid.tl1.ueln"}).

parameters.name: SpringType
parameters.description: kPerArea, kPerLine, kTot, FDefPerArea, FDefPerLine or FDefTot (force as function of extension).

parameters.name: Spring matrix form
parameters.description: Isotropic, Diagonal or Symmetric in the chosen boundary system.

parameters.name: MassType
parameters.description: mPerVolume, mPerArea, mPerLine or mTot.

tools.notes: Add Predeformation to have zero spring force at nonzero extension. Application Library: Nonlinear_Structural_Materials_Module/Hyperelasticity/thin_layer_interfaces.

tools.name: Spring-Damper (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Discrete spring and/or viscous damper between a source and a destination point, which can be geometric points, centroids of selected entities, attachments/rigid connectors, or a fixed point in space. The spring can be Directional (axial, with linear stiffness or force as a function of the extension) or a full 6-DOF matrix including translation-rotation coupling. It can connect parts in different structural interfaces.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Global > Connectors > Spring-Damper (also Multibody Dynamics, Beam, Shell). Java: physics("solid").create("spd1", "SpringDamper", -1); set("SpringFormulation", "SpringTypeDirectional"); set("SpringType", "kSpring"); set("k", "1e5[N/m]"); set("c", "50[N*s/m]").

parameters.name: Source / Destination
parameters.description: Connection point (Source Point/Destination Point subnodes), attachment, rigid connector, or Fixed.

parameters.name: SpringFormulation
parameters.description: Directional or full matrix (k_u, k_th, coupling terms).

parameters.name: SpringType, k, Fs
parameters.description: Spring constant or force as function of elongation (solid.spd1.dl).

parameters.name: c
parameters.description: Viscous damping coefficient.

tools.notes: Place it in an interface with rotational DOFs if one of the connected interfaces has them. For distributed springs use Spring Foundation or Thin Layer.

tools.name: Point Mass (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Adds a concentrated mass at a point (Isotropic, Diagonal or Symmetric mass matrix in a chosen coordinate system) to represent small attached components in dynamic, gravity or rotating-frame analyses. A checkbox can exclude it from frame acceleration forces and mass properties.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Points > Point Mass (also Beam, Truss, Wire, Shell, Multibody Dynamics). Java type string PointMass (seen with tag pm in the Beam and Wire interfaces): physics("solid").create("pm1", "PointMass", 0).

parameters.name: Point mass m
parameters.description: Mass, isotropic or as a matrix.

parameters.name: Exclude contribution
parameters.description: Exclude from Gravity, Rotating Frame, Linearly Accelerated Frame, Base Excitation and mass-property evaluation.

tools.notes: A point mass on a solid creates a singular local stress; distribute large masses with Added Mass or a Rigid Connector with Mass and Moment of Inertia.

tools.name: Added Mass (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Supplies additional inertia that is not part of the material, on domains, boundaries, edges or points: mass per reference volume, area or length, or total mass, as isotropic, diagonal or symmetric (anisotropic) matrices. Typical uses are non-structural mass such as paint, insulation, fluid contents, electrodes or thin foils.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Boundaries > Added Mass (also domains, edges, points; Shell, Layered Shell, Beam). Java: physics("solid").create("adm1", "AddedMass2", 2); set("MassType", "mPerArea"); set("mPerArea", ...).

parameters.name: MassType
parameters.description: mPerVolume, mPerArea, mPerLine or mTot depending on entity level.

parameters.name: Mass matrix form
parameters.description: Isotropic, Diagonal or Symmetric in the chosen coordinate system.

parameters.name: ExcludeFromMassForces
parameters.description: Exclude from gravity/frame accelerations and mass properties.

tools.notes: The type string numbers the entity dimension (AddedMass1 on edges in the Beam interface, AddedMass2 on boundaries).

tools.name: Predeformation (Spring Foundation)
tools.description: Subnode of Spring Foundation or Spring Material that shifts the unstressed state of the spring, so the elastic force is zero at a given nonzero displacement u0. The value may vary during the analysis, so it is a load, not an initial value; it is used for preloaded supports, springs installed with a set length and gasket preload.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Spring Foundation (or Thin Layer > Spring Material) > Predeformation. Java: feature("spf1").create("prd1", "PreDeformation", 2).

parameters.name: Spring predeformation u0
parameters.description: Displacement vector at which the spring force vanishes.

parameters.name: Load group
parameters.description: Assign the predeformation load to a load group for load cases.

tools.notes: Available also in Plate, Beam, Truss, Wire, Multibody Dynamics and explicit dynamics interfaces.

tools.name: Low-Reflecting Boundary (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Absorbing boundary for elastic waves in time-dependent and frequency-domain analyses: a viscous traction matched to the P- and S-wave impedances of the adjacent material (default 0.5*rho*(cp+cs)) lets waves leave the model with little reflection, best at normal incidence. Used for seismic, blasting, ultrasound and machine-foundation models.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Boundaries > More > Low-Reflecting Boundary (also Solid Mechanics, Explicit Dynamics). Java: physics("solid").create("lrb1", "LowReflectingBoundary", 2); set("DampingType", "PSwaves").

parameters.name: DampingType
parameters.description: PSwaves (from material) or user defined mechanical impedance d_im.

parameters.name: CalculateDissipatedEnergy
parameters.description: Accumulate energy absorbed by the boundary.

tools.notes: For better absorption in frequency domain use Perfectly Matched Layers or waveguide Ports.

tools.name: Fasteners (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Simplified modeling of rivets and bolts between plates or solids whose holes already exist in the geometry: matching holes (Hole Selection subnode, with automatic hole detection) are joined by elastic connectors either at hole edges or at annular boundaries around the holes (more accurate, lower stress concentration). A Safety subnode evaluates fastener failure, and result templates tabulate normal and shear forces per fastener.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics (or Shell) > Connectors > Fasteners > Hole Selection / Safety. Java type strings seen in the Shell interface: physics("shell").create("fst1", "Fasteners", -1); feature("fst1").create("hsel1", "HoleSelection", -1).

parameters.name: Connection type
parameters.description: Hole edges or boundaries surrounding the holes.

parameters.name: Fastener stiffness
parameters.description: Elastic properties/diameter of the fastener connector.

parameters.name: Safety subnode
parameters.description: Allowable normal/shear forces giving a damage index per fastener.

tools.notes: Re-evaluate the fastener evaluation groups when the number of fasteners changes. For spot welds in shells see Spot Welds (Shell).

tools.name: Attachment (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Defines a set of boundaries on a flexible (or rigid) domain that acts as the connection point for Multibody Dynamics joints, springs or bearings. The connection is Rigid (all selected boundaries move as one rigid body, stiffening locally) or Flexible (kinematic constraint only in an average sense, statically equivalent load distribution). Attachments also exist on shell edges and beam points.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics or Multibody Dynamics > Boundaries > Attachment. Java: physics("mbd").create("att1", "Attachment", 2); set("ConnectionType", "RigidType").

parameters.name: ConnectionType
parameters.description: RigidType or flexible.

parameters.name: groupODEs
parameters.description: How extra DOFs are grouped in the solver (fromInterface, yes, no).

tools.notes: Thermal Expansion (Attachment) subnode accounts for thermal growth of the virtual rigid body.

tools.name: Applied Force, Applied Moment and Mass (Rigid Connector)
tools.description: Subnodes of Rigid Connector (and Rigid Material) that load or add inertia to the rigid body: Applied Force at the center of rotation or a user location, Applied Moment, and Mass and Moment of Inertia (mass and inertia tensor of an unmodelled component, e.g. a motor on a bracket). Center of Rotation subnodes define the reference point by centroid of boundaries, edges or points.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Rigid Connector > Applied Force | Applied Moment | Mass and Moment of Inertia | Center of Rotation: Point. Java: feature("rig1").create("rf1", "RigidBodyForce", -1); feature("rig1").create("rm1", "RigidBodyMoment", -1); feature("rig1").create("rmm1", "RigidBodyMassInertia", -1).

parameters.name: Ft, PointOfApplicationType, Direction
parameters.description: Applied Force vector, point of application (center of rotation xc or user defined) and SpaceFixed or follower direction.

parameters.name: Mt
parameters.description: Applied Moment vector about the center of rotation.

parameters.name: mt, mi, xm
parameters.description: Mass and Moment of Inertia: mass, inertia tensor and center of mass location.

tools.notes: Parameter keys verified in Application Library models (bracket_random_vibration, shaft_with_fillet, multistudy_bracket_optimization). The same subnodes exist under Rigid Material (AppliedForce, AppliedMoment, MassInertia). See the existing Rigid Connector entry for the parent node.

tools.name: Reduced Flexible Components (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Component mode synthesis: marks flexible parts to be replaced by reduced-order models built from fixed-interface eigenmodes plus static constraint modes at the interfaces (joints, attachments). Components are detected from geometry or user defined (Component Definition subnodes, number of eigenmodes each); the Configure CMS Study button generates the model-reduction studies, and the reduced parts can then run in multibody or frequency-response analyses at a fraction of the cost.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Domains > Reduced Flexible Components > Component Definition; Component Mode Synthesis section toolbar > Configure CMS Study. Java: physics("solid").create("rfc1", "ReducedFlexibleComponents", 3); set("componentDefinition", "fromGeometry"); set("nModes", "6").

parameters.name: componentDefinition
parameters.description: fromGeometry (automatic subdivision) or user defined.

parameters.name: nModes
parameters.description: Number of eigenmodes per reduced component (overridable per Component Definition).

parameters.name: includeLoadContributions
parameters.description: Include interface loads inside the ROM (then disable them in the global study).

parameters.name: synchronizeRom
parameters.description: Keep study Solve-for settings consistent automatically.

tools.notes: Fixed Joint subnodes with Source/Destination filters connect reduced components. See Component Mode Synthesis in the user's guide and the Model Reduction study.

tools.name: Contact Methods: Penalty, Augmented Lagrangian and Nitsche (Contact)
tools.description: The Contact and Interior Contact nodes enforce non-penetration with one of three algorithms: Penalty (default; a stiff spring whose penalty factor trades accuracy for conditioning; also Penalty, dynamic with viscous regularization for transients), Augmented Lagrangian (exact enforcement via Lagrange multipliers, segregated or fully coupled, penalty preset for Stability, Speed or Bending), and Nitsche (consistent weak method using the domain tractions; symmetric, skew-symmetric or incomplete formulation). In AL and Nitsche the penalty factor affects convergence but not the final accuracy.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Pairs > Contact > Contact Method. Java: feature("dcnt1").set("ContactMethodCtrl", "Penalty" | "PenaltyDynamic" | "AugmentedLagrange" | "AugmentedLagrangeDynamic" | "Nitsche"); set("SolutionMethod", "segregated"); set("tunedFor", "Stability").

parameters.name: ContactMethodCtrl
parameters.description: Penalty, PenaltyDynamic, AugmentedLagrange, AugmentedLagrangeDynamic or Nitsche.

parameters.name: penaltyCtrlPenalty / fp_penalty / pn_penalty
parameters.description: Automatic, manual tuning (multiplier) or user-defined penalty factor; default based on solid.Eequ/h of the destination.

parameters.name: penaltyCtrlAuglag, tunedFor, useRelaxation
parameters.description: Preset tuned for Stability, Speed or Bending; relaxation strategy.

parameters.name: NitscheFormulation
parameters.description: symmetric, nonsymmetric (skew) or incomplete.

parameters.name: Offset, penaltyFunction
parameters.description: Contact surface offset and ramp or smooth-ramp penalty function.

tools.notes: Contact pairs are defined under Definitions (source should be the stiffer, coarser-meshed side). A Contact Force plot group is added to Result Templates. See the existing Contact / Contact Pair entries and the Contact Modeling chapter for solver settings.

tools.name: Interior Contact (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Simplified contact on interior boundaries of a single meshed object (for example a pre-cut crack surface, a sliding joint or a delamination plane) without creating contact pairs. It supports penalty, augmented Lagrangian and (incomplete) Nitsche methods, Friction, and Adhesion/Decohesion for cohesive-zone debonding, but is limited to small relative sliding.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Boundaries > Interior Contact (subnodes Friction, Adhesion > Decohesion). Java: physics("solid").create("icnt1", "InteriorContact", 2); set("ContactMethodCtrl", "Penalty").

parameters.name: ContactMethodCtrl
parameters.description: Penalty, AugmentedLagrange or Nitsche (incomplete only).

parameters.name: E_char, fp_penalty, pn
parameters.description: Characteristic stiffness and penalty factor control.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Contact surface offset.

tools.notes: For large sliding use Contact with pairs or General Contact. Geomechanics: deep_excavation uses Interior Contact for wall-soil interfaces.

tools.name: General Contact (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Automatic contact between any boundaries (including self-contact) defined by a General Contact Pair under Definitions, without choosing source and destination sides. It always uses the penalty method through Contact Model subnodes, with optional Friction and Damping (General Contact), No Contact exclusions and Offset subnodes. Well suited for complex assemblies, impact and large sliding, including explicit dynamics.
tools.usage: Definitions > Pairs > General Contact Pair; Solid Mechanics > Pairs > General Contact > Contact Model. Java: physics("solid").create("dgcnt1", "GeneralContact", 2); feature("dgcnt1").feature("cmod1").set("penaltyFactorMultiplier", "automatic").

parameters.name: excludeConstrainedBoundaries
parameters.description: Omit boundaries with constraints from the contact search.

parameters.name: Contact Model: penaltyStiffness
parameters.description: From material stiffness or From mass (transient).

parameters.name: Contact Model: penaltyFactorMultiplier, fp_penalty
parameters.description: Automatic, Automatic soft, or Manual tuning multiplier.

parameters.name: Contact Model: penaltyFunction
parameters.description: ramp or smooth ramp (with start location and transition size) for impact.

tools.notes: Forces geometric nonlinearity in all studies unless the default pair is disconnected. Pairs selected in several General Contact nodes are exclusive (last one wins).

tools.name: Friction (Contact)
tools.description: Subnode of Contact, Interior Contact or General Contact Model for stick-slip friction: Coulomb (friction coefficient mu), Exponential dynamic Coulomb (static and dynamic coefficients with decay coefficient over slip velocity, transient only) or User defined. A cohesion sliding resistance and a maximum tangential traction can limit the tangential stress; tangential penalty and augmented Lagrangian settings follow the parent.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Contact > Friction. Java: feature("dcnt1").create("fric1", "Friction", 2); set("FrictionModel", "Coulomb" | "DynamicCoulomb"); set("mu_fric", "0.2").

parameters.name: FrictionModel
parameters.description: Coulomb, DynamicCoulomb (exponential dynamic) or user defined.

parameters.name: mu_fric / mustat, mudyn, dcfric
parameters.description: Friction coefficient, or static/dynamic coefficients and decay coefficient.

parameters.name: cohe, Ttmax
parameters.description: Cohesion sliding resistance and maximum tangential traction (default Inf).

parameters.name: storeFricEnergy, sliptotStore
parameters.description: Store frictional dissipation and accumulated slip.

tools.notes: Friction makes the stiffness matrix unsymmetric and requires a well-defined boundary coordinate system. Only one Friction node per Contact node; Friction and Slip Velocity are mutually exclusive.

tools.name: Slip Velocity (Contact)
tools.description: Simplified friction when the slip direction and speed are known (brake discs, belt sliding, rolling with known creep): the friction traction is computed from the contact pressure and a prescribed slip velocity vector, so no stick/slip state has to be solved. Velocity-dependent friction models can therefore be used even in stationary studies.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Contact > Slip Velocity. Java: feature("dcnt1").create("sv1", "FrictionSlipVelocity", 2); set("vslip", new String[]{"omega*sys2.r", "0", "0"}); set("mu_fric", "0.45").

parameters.name: vslip
parameters.description: Slip velocity in a boundary coordinate system.

parameters.name: FrictionModel, mu_fric
parameters.description: Coulomb, exponential dynamic Coulomb or user defined; friction coefficient.

parameters.name: sliptotStore
parameters.description: Accumulate total slip (used by Wear).

tools.notes: Cannot be combined with a Friction node under the same Contact node.

tools.name: Adhesion (Contact)
tools.description: Bonds contact boundaries so they can also carry tension and shear once an activation criterion is met: Always active, contact Pressure above p0, Gap below delta0, or a User defined Boolean, with an optional reset criterion. Adhesive stiffness comes from the contact penalty factor, user values per area, or material data of a thin adhesive layer. Requires the penalty method without offset.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Contact or Interior Contact > Adhesion. Java: feature("icnt1").create("adh1", "Adhesion", 2); set("ActivationCriterion", "Always"); set("StiffnessInput", "FromPenaltyFactor").

parameters.name: ActivationCriterion, p0, delta0, activation, reset
parameters.description: When adhesion starts and when it is removed.

parameters.name: StiffnessInput
parameters.description: FromPenaltyFactor, user defined kPerArea, or material data (E, nu or K, G and layer thickness ds).

parameters.name: ShearStiffness, ntau
parameters.description: Shear stiffness as a ratio of the normal stiffness.

tools.notes: Friction settings are ignored where adhesion is active. Add Decohesion to let the bond fail.

tools.name: Decohesion (Contact)
tools.description: Cohesive zone model that degrades an adhesive bond: Displacement-based or Energy-based damage with Linear, Exponential, Polynomial or Multilinear traction-separation laws defined by tensile and shear strengths and mode I/II energy release rates. Mixed-mode propagation uses Power law, Generalized power law or Benzeggagh-Kenane criteria; optional viscous regularization stabilizes snap-back. Used for delamination, debonding of coatings and adhesive joint failure.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Contact > Decohesion (requires Adhesion), or Interior Contact > Adhesion > Decohesion. Java: feature("adh1").create("dch1", "Decohesion", 2); set("CohesiveZoneModel", "DispDamage"); set("TractionSeparationLaw", "LinearSeparation"); set("FailureCriterion", "BK").

parameters.name: CohesiveZoneModel
parameters.description: DispDamage (displacement-based) or energy-based damage.

parameters.name: TractionSeparationLaw
parameters.description: Linear, exponential, polynomial or multilinear (shape factor lambda).

parameters.name: sigmat, sigmas, Gct, Gcs
parameters.description: Tensile and shear strength; mode I and mode II energy release rates.

parameters.name: FailureCriterion, alpha
parameters.description: Mixed-mode criterion: Power, generalized power law or BK with exponent.

parameters.name: ViscousRegularization, tauv
parameters.description: None or viscous regularization with characteristic time.

tools.notes: Use load or displacement control with small steps (or Global Equations for arc-length-like control). For layered shells the Delamination node offers the same laws.

tools.name: Wear (Contact)
tools.description: Computes material removal from sliding contact in time-dependent studies using a Generalized Archard law, wear rate = k*(Tn/Tn_ref)^n*v_slip, or a user-defined rate. The worn depth is applied either by actually deforming the geometry (Deformed geometry formulation, extra DOFs and mesh smoothing) or as an offset in the contact condition (Offset-based); in shells and membranes it reduces the thickness. Wear can be computed on the destination or source side.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Contact > Wear. Java: feature("dcnt1").create("wear1", "Wear", 2); set("wearFormulation", "deformedGeometry"); set("wearModel", "GeneralizedArchard"); set("k", "1e-14"); set("WearSurface", "Destination").

parameters.name: wearFormulation
parameters.description: deformedGeometry or offset-based.

parameters.name: wearModel, k, Tn_ref, n
parameters.description: Generalized Archard wear constant, reference pressure and exponent (n = 1 classical Archard).

parameters.name: WearSurface
parameters.description: Destination (more accurate) or Source; add two nodes to wear both.

tools.notes: Ignored in non-transient studies; use accelerated wear constants and Slip Velocity for long service times. Not available in the Layered Shell interface.

tools.name: Stabilization (Contact)
tools.description: Subnode of Contact (and Bolt Thread Contact) that adds temporary springs to suppress rigid-body motion of parts that are held only by contact which is not yet established in stationary/quasistatic analyses. Springs act on adjacent domains, contact boundaries or between the contact pairs; the Automatic method relaxes them after contact is detected so the final result is unaffected, while Manual gives explicit control.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Contact > Stabilization. Java: feature("dcnt1").create("stb1", "ContactStabilization", 2); set("applyTo", "adjacentDomains"); set("method", "manual"); set("stiffnessMultiplier", "1").

parameters.name: applyTo
parameters.description: adjacentDomains, contact boundaries or contact pairs.

parameters.name: stiffnessMultiplier
parameters.description: Scale of the estimated stabilization stiffness k_char.

parameters.name: method, activation, stabilizationCondition
parameters.description: Automatic or manual relaxation, e.g. active only in the first iteration of the first step.

tools.notes: Check reaction forces to verify that stabilization has been relaxed. Membrane has its own Stabilization node for wrinkling-free prestress states.

tools.name: Bolt Pretension (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Defines pretension in bolts modeled as solids (3D and 2D axisymmetric) or beams, given as Pretension force, Pretension stress or Tightening torque (with nominal/hole/thread diameters, head size, thread angle, lead and friction coefficients). Each bolt is picked by a Bolt Selection subnode (cut boundary of the shank); sequential tightening and relaxation are supported. The pretension is established by a Bolt Pretension study step before service loads are applied.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Global > Bolt Pretension > Bolt Selection; Study > Bolt Pretension. Java: physics("solid").create("pblt1", "BoltPrestress", -1); set("preTensionType", "PreTensionForce"); set("F_pre", "10[kN]"); feature("pblt1").feature("sblt1").selection().set(new int[]{...}).

parameters.name: preTensionType
parameters.description: PreTensionForce (F_pre), pretension stress (s_pre) or tightening torque (M_pre).

parameters.name: db, dh, dt, boltHead, alpha, l, muh, mut
parameters.description: Geometry and friction data for torque-tension conversion (computeTorque).

parameters.name: Bolt Selection: boltLabel, seqTight, relax
parameters.description: Per-bolt label, sequential tightening and relaxation options.

tools.notes: Requires the Structural Mechanics Module. Combine with Contact (with Friction) between clamped parts; see the Bolt Pretension study entry.

tools.name: Bolt Thread Contact (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Simplified contact model for mating threads represented by smooth cylindrical surfaces: the thread flank geometry (half thread angle, lead, handedness, contact orientation up/down) and friction are included analytically, so realistic bolt load transfer and loosening torque are captured without meshing the helix. One node per bolt, using a contact pair with the internal thread as source.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Pairs > Bolt Thread Contact (Stabilization subnode available). Java: physics("solid").create("btc1", "PairBoltThreadContact", 2); set("alpha", "30[deg]"); set("l", "1.25[mm]"); set("orient", "Right"); set("mu", "0.1").

parameters.name: alpha
parameters.description: Half thread angle (30 deg for ISO/UTS).

parameters.name: l, orient
parameters.description: Lead and handedness (3D).

parameters.name: bolt_geom, d_p, e_a, p_axis
parameters.description: Automatic or user-defined bolt diameter and axis.

parameters.name: cnt_orient, mu, pn
parameters.description: Contact orientation (Both/Up/Down), friction coefficient, penalty factor.

tools.notes: Available in 3D and 2D axisymmetry. Combine with Bolt Pretension (tightening torque).

tools.name: Crack (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Declares boundaries as a crack for linear elastic fracture mechanics: Slit (an interior boundary whose sides are disconnected), From geometry (two physical faces) or Symmetric (half model with the crack on a symmetry plane). A crack may have several fronts and branches; J-Integral and Virtual Crack Extension subnodes evaluate energy release rates and stress intensity factors, Face Load applies crack-face pressure, and Crack Closure handles contact between crack faces.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Boundaries > Fracture > Crack. Java: physics("solid").create("crack1", "Crack", 2); set("CrackSurface", "Slit"); feature("crack1").create("jint1", "JIntegral", 1).

parameters.name: CrackSurface
parameters.description: Slit, From geometry (select Crack Face 1) or Symmetric (select crack front).

parameters.name: CrackOrientation
parameters.description: FromCrack or user defined via a coordinate system.

parameters.name: Subnodes
parameters.description: J-Integral, Virtual Crack Extension, Face Load (Crack), Crack Closure, Reverse Crack Front.

tools.notes: Requires the Structural Mechanics Module. Use a refined, preferably structured mesh around the front; the crack size variable solid.crack1.crackSize sets default path radii.

tools.name: J-Integral (Crack)
tools.description: Crack subnode that evaluates the J-integral on a circular path around each crack-front point (2D: circular or along selected edges; 3D: many circular paths along the front) and derives stress intensity factors K_I, K_II (and K_III in 3D) using an additional mode separation. Paths should avoid other boundaries, holes and loads; several radii are recommended to check path independence.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Crack > J-Integral. Java: feature("crack1").create("jint1", "JIntegral", 0); set("IntegrationPath", "Circular"); set("r", "solid.crack1.crackSize*0.5").

parameters.name: IntegrationPath
parameters.description: Circular or On edges (2D).

parameters.name: r
parameters.description: Radius of the contour integral (default half the estimated crack size).

parameters.name: b, c
parameters.description: Region for separating stress intensity factors (0.2 and 0.5 of crack size).

parameters.name: NGamma, NArea
parameters.description: Number of integration points on the contour and area.

tools.notes: J-integral assumes linear elastic (or nonlinear elastic) material and quasistatic loading; for more general cases use Virtual Crack Extension.

tools.name: Virtual Crack Extension (Crack)
tools.description: Crack subnode that computes the energy release rate and stress intensity factors by a sensitivity analysis in which the crack front is virtually advanced (a Deformed Geometry region of radius R_s). It is more versatile than the J-integral (e.g. thermal loads, cracks near boundaries) and generates a dedicated study that can include a parametric sweep of the crack length.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Crack > Virtual Crack Extension (creates a sensitivity-based study). Java: feature("crack1").create("vce1", "VirtualCrackExtension", 1); set("R", "0.5*solid.crack1.crackSize"); set("parametricStudy", "yes").

parameters.name: Crack front
parameters.description: Edges (3D) or point (2D) at which G is evaluated.

parameters.name: R
parameters.description: Radius of the sensitivity (virtually moved) region.

parameters.name: b, c
parameters.description: Bounds of the region used to separate stress intensity factors.

parameters.name: parametricStudy, parameterName, parameterRange
parameters.description: Optional sweep, e.g. of crack length.

tools.notes: Requires the Structural Mechanics Module; uses the Sensitivity study functionality.

tools.name: Stress Linearization (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Defines stress classification lines (SCL) and computes membrane, bending and peak stress components and their equivalent values along them, as required by pressure-vessel codes (ASME BPVC Section VIII Div. 2, EN 13445). The SCL can be a single line (edges or two points/coordinates) or Distributed from selected boundaries through the domain; adding or changing it only needs Update Solution.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Global > Stress Linearization; Results > Line Segments plots Membrane / Membrane plus Bending stress. Java: physics("solid").create("sl1", "StressLinearization", -1); set("TypeSelection", "Distributed" | "Line"); set("lineSelection", "Edge").

parameters.name: TypeSelection
parameters.description: Line or Distributed.

parameters.name: lineSelection, StartPointDefinition, EndPointDefinition
parameters.description: SCL defined by Edge or by two Points/Coordinates (pt0, pt1).

parameters.name: Axis orientation / reference point
parameters.description: Local system for 2D axisymmetric and 3D evaluations.

tools.notes: Does not affect the solution. The SCL should cross the wall thickness from one free boundary to another.

tools.name: Section Forces (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Integrates stresses over a planar cut through a solid to give beam-like section forces in a local system: axial force N, shear forces T1 and T2, twisting moment Mt and bending moments M1 and M2. Results appear in a Section Forces evaluation group and arrow plots; enabling Compute boundary fluxes gives higher accuracy. Useful for connecting 3D stress results to hand calculations or code checks.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Global > Section Forces (select planar boundaries, optionally disconnected). Java: physics("solid").create("secf1", "SectionForces", -1); set("sys", "sys1"); set("DisconnectedBoundaries", "0").

parameters.name: Cut plane selection
parameters.description: Planar boundaries in one plane; Allow disconnected boundaries option.

parameters.name: sys
parameters.description: Coordinate system defining the local section axes.

parameters.name: SymmetryPlane, SymmetryType
parameters.description: Account for a symmetry plane when the section is cut by it.

tools.notes: Only needs Update Solution after adding. For beams, section forces are native variables (beam.Nxl, beam.Mzl...).

tools.name: Warpage and Average Rotation (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Warpage measures the out-of-plane deviation of a (usually initially flat) surface after removing an average rigid-body motion or relative to a reference plane, for PCBs, wafers and molded parts. Average Rotation computes the least-squares rigid rotation and displacement (with velocities and accelerations) of a set of points about a chosen center of rotation. Both use Small rotations or finite-rotation models (symmetric segregated or unsymmetric coupled).
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Boundaries > Warpage; Solid Mechanics > Global > Average Rotation. Java: physics("solid").create("wrp1", "Warpage", 2); set("RotationModel", "SmallRotation"); physics("solid").create("avgr1", "AverageRotation", -1); set("RotationModel", "FiniteRotationSym").

parameters.name: RotationModel
parameters.description: SmallRotation, FiniteRotationSym (symmetric segregated) or unsymmetric coupled.

parameters.name: ReferencePlane (Warpage)
parameters.description: Average rigid motion or plane from points.

parameters.name: CenterOfRotation (Average Rotation)
parameters.description: Automatic, centroid of selected entities, or user defined.

tools.notes: Small-rotation versions only define variables (Update Solution suffices); finite-rotation versions add equations and need re-solving.

tools.name: Adiabatic Heating (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Computes the temperature rise from fast dissipative deformation without a separate heat transfer interface: rho*Cp*dT/dt = beta_ah*Q_h, where Q_h collects plastic, creep, viscoplastic or other dissipation. It is used for high-rate forming, impact and machining, where heat has no time to conduct, and feeds thermal softening of Johnson-Cook type hardening.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Domains > Adiabatic Heating (also Adiabatic Heating, Layered in Shell/Membrane).

parameters.name: T_ini
parameters.description: Initial temperature (default 293.15 K).

parameters.name: Cp
parameters.description: Heat capacity at constant pressure (From material).

parameters.name: beta_ah
parameters.description: Coefficient of adiabatic heating (fraction of dissipation converted to heat, default 1).

parameters.name: Dissipative heat source
parameters.description: Include all dissipative sources or user defined (e.g. solid.Wc, solid.Wvp).

tools.example:
Solid Mechanics > Adiabatic Heating 1 (all domains), beta_ah = 0.9
Linear Elastic Material 1 > Plasticity 1: Johnson-Cook with power-law thermal softening
Study: Time Dependent or Explicit Dynamics
tools.notes: Energy dissipation must be computed in the material node. For conduction and convection use Thermal Stress with Heat Transfer instead.

tools.name: Elastic Predeformation (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Enables incremental solution of large elastic deformations with the deformed-geometry functionality: each step solves on a material frame already deformed by the previous total displacement u_pd, with the corresponding initial stress, which can greatly speed up very large deformation problems. Total displacements are available as u_tot_old and u_tot; the predeformation gradient can also be user defined, e.g. withsol('sol1', solid.FdxX).
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > <material> > Elastic Predeformation.

parameters.name: Predeformation gradient
parameters.description: From material frame (default) or User defined.

parameters.name: Store deformation history
parameters.description: Store the step displacement in u_pd for the next step.

parameters.name: Set up deformed geometry
parameters.description: Let the material frame follow u_pd from the previous step.

tools.example:
Solid Mechanics > Hyperelastic Material 1 > Elastic Predeformation 1 (defaults)
Study: Stationary with parametric sweep of the load in several increments; plot solid.u_tot
tools.notes: Available for 3D, 2D and 2D axisymmetry; only elastic behavior is transferred between steps.

tools.name: Port (Solid Mechanics)
tools.description: Excites and absorbs elastic waves in waveguide structures (3D only), one propagating mode per Port node, and computes S-parameters. Mode shapes come from a Boundary Mode Analysis study (Numeric port); several ports on the same boundary (longitudinal, torsional, flexural) together give an almost perfectly non-reflecting termination, better than PML or Low-Reflecting Boundary.
tools.usage: Solid Mechanics > Boundaries > Port; Study: Boundary Mode Analysis + Frequency Domain. Java: physics("solid").create("port1", "Port", 2); set("PortType", "Numeric"); set("PortExcitation", "on").

parameters.name: PortName, PortType
parameters.description: Port identifier and type (Numeric from boundary mode analysis).

parameters.name: PortExcitation, IncidentWave, power, phi
parameters.description: Whether the port is excited, incident amplitude/power and phase.

tools.notes: Include every propagating mode with cutoff inside the frequency range. Mode shapes are normalized to 1 W apparent power.
